title: Story Steps: Read It Twice
child_idea: Read a story twice. Then write one number sentence for each step: add, or take away.

Write one number sentence for each step of a two-step story (add or take away within 100) and answer in a sentence.
Choose add or take away from the words of the story (gets, gives away, more than, fewer than), not from the order of the numbers.
Play Mi's Challenge Quest, a game with Mi on private paper: 8 short gates that visit the lessons of the term.

Story words: which words mean add and which mean take away
Adding and taking away tens and ones: 40 + 20, 37 + 10, 56 - 20, 24 + 5

lines.text: Greet the whole group warmly, before the recording starts. Check that you can see each child, or ask the grown-up.

Hello, inquirers! Last lesson of the term. Pencil, paper, counters and your workbook on the table, please. Today we read stories twice, and after our break and our workbook we play Mi's Challenge Quest.
This lesson is recorded so a friend who is away can catch up. The recording has me, the shared screen and any voice that is not muted. You may keep your microphone and camera off.
Start the recording now. Do not use children's first names on the recording.
@rec
Microphone off until I ask you to speak. To answer, say it with me on three, show fingers, or give a thumbs up. Nobody holds paper up to the camera.
Greet the whole group warmly. Do not use children's first names on the recording.

Lesson 10 only: say once that Mi's Challenge Quest is a game on private paper, with a quest partner beside you, and not a race. The routine and the four inquirer rules were taught in Lesson 1; for a new child one sentence is enough: notice it, test it, explain why, mistakes help us. Say the recording statement and the microphone routine in the same words every lesson.
@rec
I think of a number. Use your fingers or counters to find it. I add 3, and I get 8. What is my number?
I take away 2, and I get 6. What was my number?
I add 10, and I get thirty-five. What was my number?
Story words. Gets, finds and buys mean add. Gives away, eats and loses mean take away.
Siti eats 3 sweets. Add or take away?
Ali finds 5 more shells. Add or take away?
Mei gives away 2 stickers. Add or take away?
4 more children join the line. Add or take away?
Tens and ones, quickly. Think of bundles of ten.
Forty plus twenty?
Thirty-seven plus ten?
Fifty-six take away twenty?
Twenty-four plus five?
Story to number sentence. Ben has 6 cards. He gets 4 more. Which number sentence fits: 6 plus 4, or 6 take away 4?
Which one fits? And what is the answer?
Siti has 9 beads and loses 3. Which sentence, and the answer?
Ali has 12 marbles and wins 5. Which sentence, and the answer?
If a child hesitates on 47 or 36, say the tens word slowly (forty... seven) and point to the bundles: 37 + 10 is one more bundle.

Answers: 5, 8, 25; take away, add, take away, add; 60, 47, 36, 29; then 6 + 4 = 10, 9 - 3 = 6, 12 + 5 = 17. Children answer with fingers, thumbs or a whispered number. Nobody writes. A child new to tens and ones sees the bundles on the slide first.
@rec
Two sneak-peek puzzles: ideas we have not learnt yet. A guess is a great start. Nobody is judged.
Puzzle one. Ali has 4 marbles. Ben has 3 more marbles than Ali. How many marbles does Ben have? You may draw them.
Children draw or write the number on their own paper.
Puzzle two. How many marbles do Ali and Ben have altogether? Write the number. Then write what you did first.
Children write or draw their answer.
Thank you. Keep your paper and your own answer: nobody shows it. We will come back to puzzle two later, and you can check your own thinking then.

Puzzle 1 answer: 7. Puzzle 2 answer: 11 (first Ben has 4 + 3 = 7, then 4 + 7). Look for good ideas to praise later (a drawing of two groups, or a child who said Ben first). Do not write scores or keep a list.
@rec
Today your counters are the teachers. I read a story twice. You act it out, one step at a time.
Story A. Mei has 8 buttons. She gets 5 more buttons. Then she gives away 6 buttons. How many buttons does Mei have now?
Mei has 8 buttons. She gets 5 more buttons. Then she gives away 6 buttons.
Round 1: children act out story A with counters or the kit squares and show a thumbs up when done.
How many buttons does Mei have now? What did you do first?
Read it twice. First read: who is in the story and what happens? Second read: which numbers, and what is the question?
Story B. Ravi has 12 stickers. He gives 5 stickers to Siti. Then he finds 3 more stickers. How many stickers does Ravi have now?
Round 2: children act out story B with counters, one step at a time.
How many stickers does Ravi have now? Which step came first?
Story C. Ben has 9 balls. Mei has 4 more balls than Ben. How many balls do they have altogether?
Ben has 9 balls. Mei has 4 more balls than Ben.
Round 3: children build Ben's pile, then Mei's pile that is 4 more, then put both together.
How many balls does Mei have? How many do they have altogether?
Mei has more, so Mei has the greater number. Find Mei first. Then put both piles together.
What did you notice? How many steps did each story have? Did each step add or take away?
Each step is one thing: one add or one take away. Step 2 starts from the answer to Step 1.
A child who loses count: put the first number out, then add or remove counters one step at a time and say the new total after each step. A child with too few counters: use the kit squares.

Answers: story A 7 (8 + 5 = 13, then 13 - 6 = 7); story B 10 (12 - 5 = 7, then 7 + 3 = 10); story C: Mei 13, together 22 (9 + 4 = 13, then 9 + 13 = 22). Main room only: no breakout rooms. Building with counters is for every child.
@rec
Our trick: read it twice, then one number sentence for each step.
How many number sentences do we write for a story with two steps?

Mei has 26 stickers. Ali gives her 10 more stickers. Then she gives 5 stickers to Ben. Step 1: she gets more, so add. Twenty-six plus ten is thirty-six. Step 2: she gives away, so take away. Thirty-six take away five is thirty-one.
Where did the thirty-six come from?
Your turn. Siti has 40 beads. She uses 20 beads for a bracelet. Then she buys 7 more beads. How many beads does Siti have now? Write Step 1 and Step 2.
Children write two number sentences on their own paper. Wait until most have stopped writing.
Forty take away twenty is twenty. Twenty plus seven is twenty-seven.
More than and fewer than. Ali has 14. Ben has 5 more, so Ben has 19. Ben has 5 fewer, so Ben has 9. Ask: who has more?
Ben has 5 more than Ali, and Ali has 14. Does Ben have more or fewer?
Your turn. Mei has 38 stickers. Siti has 6 fewer stickers than Mei. How many stickers does Siti have? Write the number sentence.
Children write one number sentence on their own paper. Wait until most have stopped writing.
Thirty-eight take away six is thirty-two. Siti has thirty-two stickers.
Who has more, Mei or Siti? How do you know?
A trap! Ravi is in a line. 5 children are in front of Ravi and 2 are behind him. How many children are in the line? Count Ravi too: 5 plus 2 plus 1 is 8.
Children line up counters on the table: 5 in front, one for Ravi, 2 behind. They count every counter and show a thumbs up.
Who is in the group? Did we count everyone?
If a child reads fewer than as add: ask who has more, and who has the greater number. If a child leaves Ravi out: put counters in a line on the shared slide or whiteboard and touch each one.

Key words to use every time: step, read it twice, more than, fewer than, number sentence. Do not teach bar strips (Lesson 12). Keep every Start here step within 100 and without renaming; the Think harder page has the first renaming.
@rec
Stand up and sip some water. Lean forward to add, lean back to take away, in the space you have. Add 3, take away 2, add 4, take away 5. Where do you end up?
Call the four moves. Children lean forward and back in their chair or standing, in the space they have. Say each count clearly; children count quietly along. Everyone ends back upright: 3, 1, 5, 0.
@rec

Page 1, Start here. Question 1: Ben has 30 cards. He gives 20 cards away. After that, he gets 6 more cards. Fill in the steps. Question 2: Mei has 42 stickers. She gets 7 more stickers. Then she gives 10 stickers to Ali. Write one number sentence for each step. Then write how many stickers Mei has now. Question 3: Ravi has 25 pencils. He buys 10 more pencils. Then he loses 3 pencils. Circle the two number sentences that fit the story. The four sentences are: 25 plus 10 equals 35; 25 take away 10 equals 15; 35 take away 3 equals 32; 35 plus 3 equals 38.

Page 1, questions 1 to 3. Tutor looks around the gallery, asks how do you know. Wait 10 seconds before helping. Move to the answer slide only when most children have stopped writing; anyone not finished keeps going and checks later.

Answers for page 1. If you are still working, carry on and check later. Question 1: ten, then sixteen. Question 2: forty-nine, then thirty-nine. Question 3: circle 25 plus 10 and 35 take away 3. Ravi has thirty-two. Check your own page in another colour.

Page 2. Question 4: write plus or minus in each box. Ali has 8 shells and finds 5 more. Siti has 9 sweets and eats 3. Mei has 10 stickers and gives away 4. There are 12 children in a line and 6 more join. Question 5: Ali has 23 marbles. Ben has 10 more than Ali. How many marbles altogether? Question 6: A bus has 30 children. 10 children get off. Then 4 children get on. Siti writes 30 plus 10 equals 40 for Step 1. Is Siti correct? Circle Yes or No. Then find how many children are on the bus now.
Page 2, questions 4 to 6. Move to the answer slide only when most children have stopped writing.

Answers for page 2. If you are still working, carry on and check later. Question 4: plus, minus, minus, plus. Question 5: Ben has thirty-three. They have fifty-six. Question 6: no. Children who get off leave the bus, so take away. Thirty take away ten is twenty. Twenty plus four is twenty-four.
When you have finished Start here, you can choose Think harder, Go further or the Investigation. Everyone may choose. You can take pages 3 to 5 home.
Choice time: Think harder (page 3), Go further (page 4), the Investigation (page 5), or finish and check your own work. Tutor never says who is on which page.

Q1: say what happens first; gives away means take away. Q2: use counters, one step at a time. Q3: ask which sentence starts from the answer of the first. Q4: does the word make it greater or smaller? Q5: find Ben first. Q6: ask who leaves the bus.

Think harder T1: Ravi has more, so Mei has fewer; draw two groups. T2: draw the line and touch each child, Mei too. T3: find Mei first, then Siti. T4: do step 1, then ask if there is enough for step 2. Go further: write one step at a time.

A child who is still stuck ticks I am still stuck on their own look-back page. The grown-up may photograph that page and send it to the business WhatsApp after class. Open the next term with one short catch-up question for the whole group. Never a private message to a child, never a private room.

Think harder is for ideas taught today in a new setting (reversed wording, the group trap). Go further is mastery and extension. Do not announce who is on which page. Pairs are never split unless both children agree. Start here pages 1 and 2 are the target; the rest of the workbook time is for choosing, and pages 3 to 5 may go home.
@rec
Siti has 20 stickers. Ali has 5 fewer stickers than Siti. A child says Ali has 25 stickers. Do you agree? Use counters to explain.
Build 20 and take 5 away with your counters. Is Ravi right?
Talk to the grown-up next to you or to your screen for one minute. Use the sentence starter: I think... because...
Who would like to share? Volunteers first. A pass is always fine.
Remember puzzle two? Ben has 3 more than Ali, and Ali has 4. Ben has seven. Together they have eleven.
Did anyone change their mind about puzzle two while we worked? You can just nod.
Model answer: No. Fewer means less. Ali has 20 - 5 = 15. Volunteers first; never call a child by name to answer; no tallies, no rankings. Praise the reason, not the speed.
@rec

Now it is time for Mi's Challenge Quest! Mi the dolphin is swimming to the Pearl Cave, and eight gates are in the way. At each gate there is a puzzle for you. You work on your own paper with your quest partner beside you.
It is a game, not a race, and nobody gets a score. You may skip a gate and Mi will swim round it. I will not say any answers, and I will not show anyone's paper.

Pause the recording. Children take out the closed Quest Log, a pencil and a ruler. Quest partners sit beside the child and may talk about how to start, but do not give answers. Paper flat on the table, never held up. Name on page 1.

Page 1. Gate 1. Look at the sticks. How many bundles of ten, and how many single sticks? Write them. Then write how many sticks there are altogether. Gate 2. Fill in the blanks. Part a: look at the number line. Which number is the arrow pointing to? Part b: count on in tens and write the next number: 14, 24, 34.

Children work quietly on page 1 (gates 1 and 2); partners may whisper about how, not about the answer. Look around the gallery; say nothing about right or wrong. If asked, re-read a gate to the whole group.
Gates one and two are open! Mi swims on. Turn to page 2.

Gate 3. You have two cards, 3 and 8. Use both cards to make the greatest number you can. Write it. Gate 4. Look at the ten frames: 7 and 5. Write 7 plus 5. Then write 37 plus 5. Gate 5. Part a: write 52 plus 30. Part b: write 74 take away 31.
Children work quietly on page 2 (gates 3 to 5).
Gates three, four and five are open!
One-minute stretch: stand, shake out your hands, sip some water. Paper stays on the table.
Turn to page 3. You need your ruler for gate 7.

Gate 6. Fill in the missing number in each box. Part a: 8 plus 4 equals 6 plus box. Part b: 60 plus 10 equals 50 plus box. Gate 7. Use your ruler. Part a: draw a line 6 centimetres long, starting at the dot. Part b: write how long a line 4 centimetres longer than your line is.
Children work quietly on page 3 (gates 6 and 7).
Gates six and seven are open! The Pearl Cave is just ahead. Turn to page 4.

Gate 8. Read it twice. Mei has 35 stickers. Ali gives her 10 more stickers. Then she gives 3 stickers to Ben. Write a number sentence for Step 1 and for Step 2. The last number you write is how many stickers Mei has now. The secret cave has one more puzzle, and it is optional. You may skip it. Ali is in a line. There are 5 children in front of him and 3 children behind him. How many children are in the line?
Children work quietly on page 4: gate 8, then the optional secret cave item if they wish.

You reached the Pearl Cave! Make sure your name is on page 1 and close your Quest Log. Well done for trying your best. Grown-ups, please take one photo of each page today and send them to the business WhatsApp, as in the note. Mi's tutor will send you one line about what we saw, never a mark.
Say nothing about answers. Remind the group that nothing is added up and no answer is read out. Restart the recording. Children who did not finish may use the flex time at the end.

A child who says they cannot do a gate: say to the whole group that skipping is fine, Mi swims round it, and they may come back. A child who is upset: the grown-up may stop at any time; do not single the child out. Never give a hint to one child about an answer.

The answers, your private notes sheet for each child, the group advice sheet and the one-line templates for the grown-up are in L10_Quest_Tutor_Notes.pdf. Do not collect or look at any paper during the lesson. Photos arrive only on the program's business WhatsApp and the line goes to the parent only; never a message to a child, and never a personal phone. The exit ticket on workbook page 5 is for home this lesson: the quest takes its place in class.
@rec
Look-back. Tick what was hard and what helped you. Write or draw one thing you did well. If you still need help, tick I am still stuck and show your grown-up. You can pass. Nobody reads it out.
Children fill in the look-back box on page 5.
@rec
Well done, inquirers, for the whole term. Next term starts with Term 2 Lesson 1, Who Is Where? Your tutor will tell you the start date.

Please have your Term 2 Lesson 1 workbook with its cards page cut out by a grown-up (the place cards and the number cards), ten small things to put in a row (toys, cups or shoes), a coin or button, a small paper that says FRONT, a pencil and paper. Keep the cards in an envelope.
Optional, only if you are on time: Ali has 20 marbles. He wins 6 and loses 4. Does it matter which comes first?
Short think time, then take two answers.

Optional exit ticket. Question 1: a bus has 25 children. 10 children get off. Then 3 children get on. How many children are on the bus now? Question 2: Ben has 6 stickers. Mei has 5 more stickers than Ben. How many stickers does Mei have? Question 3: Siti has 20 beads. Ali has 7 fewer beads than Siti. How many beads does Ali have?
Children answer E1 to E3 on page 5 on their own.
Eighteen. Eleven. Thirteen. Check your own ticket in a different colour.
Spare-time menu. If the whole class is ahead, pick one or two activities from the guide (about 4 minutes each).

This is the standing buffer. A child who needs more time for the quest may use it. If you are behind, finish the look-back and say goodbye. Do not start anything new. Goodbye, and thank you to the grown-ups.

slides.subtitle: Read it twice: addition and subtraction in stories

mascot.say: Hi, I'm Mi. Let's notice, test and explain why!

slides.title: Warm-up: I think of a number

blocks.text: Use your fingers or counters

cols.text: I think of a number. I add 3. I get 8.

slides.note: Say: I think of a number, I add 3, I get 8. Children use fingers or counters to find the number: 5 (8 take away 3). Then: I think of a number, I take away 2, I get 6 (answer 8). Then: I think of a number, I add 10, I get 35 (answer 25). This is the holiday-course game I think of a number, used only as a warm-up; no writing.

slides.title: Story words

rows: gives away, eats, loses, leaves, how many left

blocks.text: Add or take away? Say it.

slides.note: Read the two rows aloud, then ask: Siti eats 3 sweets (take away). Ali finds 5 more shells (add). Mei gives away 2 stickers (take away). 4 more children join (add). Children answer aloud or with a thumb up for add and down for take away. Say that today we also meet the words more than and fewer than.

slides.title: Tens and ones, quickly

blocks.text: Say the answers. Think of tens and ones.

slides.note: Answers: 60, 47, 36, 29. Show 37 as 3 bundles and 7 singles: 37 + 10 is one more bundle, 47. 56 - 20 takes 2 bundles, 36. 24 + 5 adds 5 singles, 29. This is spiral review of adding and taking away tens and ones, so a child who joins cold can do the lesson. Say the tens word slowly: forty-seven.

slides.title: Story to number sentence

blocks.text: Ben has 6 cards. He gets 4 more.
Which one fits the story?

slides.note: Read each short story twice and ask which number sentence fits, then the answer. Ben has 6 cards and gets 4 more: 6 + 4 = 10. Siti has 9 beads and loses 3: 9 - 3 = 6. Ali has 12 marbles and wins 5: 12 + 5 = 17. Children answer aloud or show a thumb up for the first sentence and down for the second. No writing yet.

slides.title: Sneak-peek puzzles

blocks.text: Ideas we have not learnt yet. A guess is a great start. Nobody is judged.

cols.head: PUZZLE 1: anyone can try
items: Ali has 4 marbles.
Ben has 3 more marbles than Ali.
How many marbles does Ben have?
You may draw them.

cols.head: PUZZLE 2: think
items: How many marbles do Ali and Ben have altogether?
Write the number. Then write what you did first.

slides.note: Puzzle 1 is an access question: any child can draw 4 marbles and 3 more, and count. Puzzle 2 is the thinking question on the key idea (two steps). Say: two sneak-peek puzzles, ideas we have not learnt yet; a guess is a great start and I do not know is welcome; nobody is marked. Children write on their own paper and nobody holds paper up to the camera: children keep their own answer and check it at Talk time. Do not read answers aloud. Puzzle 1 answer 7; puzzle 2 answer 11, first Ben has 4 + 3 = 7.

slides.title: Explore: act it out

items: Listen once. Picture the story.
Listen again. Put out counters for the first number.
Do each step with your counters.
Say: how many now?

blocks.head: STORY A
items: Mei has 8 buttons. She gets 5 more buttons. Then she gives away 6 buttons.

slides.note: Round 1, about 3 minutes, objects first and no writing. Read story A twice: Mei has 8 buttons. She gets 5 more buttons. Then she gives away 6 buttons. How many buttons does Mei have now? Children act it out with counters or the kit squares: 8 and 5 more is 13, then 6 away leaves 7. Ask for a thumbs up when each child has finished. Answer for the tutor: 7.

slides.title: Read it twice

cols.head: FIRST READ
items: Who is in the story?
What happens?
No numbers yet.

cols.head: SECOND READ
items: Which numbers?
What is the question?
One step at a time.

blocks.head: STORY B
items: Ravi has 12 stickers. He gives 5 stickers to Siti. Then he finds 3 more stickers.

slides.note: Round 2, about 3 minutes. Read story B twice, with a first read for who and what, then a second read for the numbers and the question: Ravi has 12 stickers. He gives 5 stickers to Siti. Then he finds 3 more stickers. How many stickers does Ravi have now? Children act it out: 12 - 5 = 7, then 7 + 3 = 10. Answer for the tutor: 10. Praise the two reads, not the speed.

slides.title: Who has more?

blocks.head: STORY C
items: Ben has 9 balls. Mei has 4 more balls than Ben.
How many balls do they have altogether?

blocks.text: Find Mei first. Then put them together.

slides.note: Round 3, about 3 minutes. Read story C twice: Ben has 9 balls. Mei has 4 more balls than Ben. How many balls do they have altogether? Children act it out with counters: a pile of 9 for Ben, then a pile for Mei that is 4 more (13), then put both piles together (22). Answer for the tutor: Mei 13, together 22. Say that Mei has more, so her pile is the greater one. This sets up question 5 in the workbook.

slides.title: What did we notice?

items: How many steps did each story have?
Did each step add, or take away?
Where did Step 2 start?

slides.note: Take one or two answers from volunteers. Key ideas: each story had two steps; each step was one add or one take away; Step 2 starts from the answer to Step 1. Repeat a child's answer in your own words so the recording picks it up. This sets up the mini-lesson.

slides.title: Read it twice, then step by step

cols.head: FIRST READ
items: Who? What happens?

cols.head: SECOND READ
items: Which numbers? What is asked?

blocks.text: One step, one number sentence

slides.note: Name the routine: read it twice, then write one number sentence for each step. First read: who and what, no numbers. Second read: the numbers and the question. Then each step is one add or one take away. Ask: how many number sentences for a two-step story? Answer: two.

slides.title: Mei's stickers

blocks.head: STORY
items: Mei has 26 stickers. Ali gives her 10 more stickers. Then she gives 5 stickers to Ben. How many stickers does Mei have now?

slides.note: Think aloud. First read: Mei, stickers, Ali gives, she gives to Ben. Second read: 26, 10 more, 5 to Ben. Step 1: gets more, so add, 26 + 10 = 36 (one more bundle of ten). Step 2: gives away, so take away, 36 - 5 = 31 (no renaming: 6 - 5 = 1). Write the answer in a sentence. Ask: where did 36 come from? Answer: from Step 1.

slides.title: Your turn: two steps

blocks.text: Write Step 1 and Step 2 on your paper. About 1 minute.

blocks.head: STORY
items: Siti has 40 beads. She uses 20 beads for a bracelet. Then she buys 7 more beads. How many beads does Siti have now?

slides.note: Read the story twice. Each child writes on their own paper; wait until most children have stopped writing. Do not ask children to hold boards up in front of the group. Answer for the tutor: 40 - 20 = 20, then 20 + 7 = 27.

slides.title: Check: two steps

blocks.text: Siti has 27 beads.

slides.note: Answers: 40 - 20 = 20 and 20 + 7 = 27. Read each answer aloud so a child watching the recording can mark their own work. Ask: which words told us to take away? (uses) And to add? (buys more).

slides.title: More than, fewer than

rows: Ben has 5 more than Ali. Ali has 14.
Ben has 5 fewer than Ali. Ali has 14.

blocks.text: Ask: who has more?

slides.note: More than and fewer than compare two people. Ali has 14. Ben has 5 more, so Ben has 14 + 5 = 19. Ben has 5 fewer, so Ben has 14 - 5 = 9. Always ask who has more. Then the person with more has the greater number. Keep it to one minute; the reversed wording (Ravi has more, find Mei) is for Think harder.

slides.title: Your turn: fewer than

blocks.text: Who has more? Write the number sentence. About 1 minute.

blocks.head: STORY
items: Mei has 38 stickers. Siti has 6 fewer stickers than Mei. How many stickers does Siti have?

slides.note: Read the story twice. Each child writes on their own paper; wait until most children have stopped writing. Do not ask children to hold boards up in front of the group. Answer for the tutor: 38 - 6 = 32.

slides.title: Check: fewer than

blocks.text: Siti has 32 stickers.

slides.note: Answer: 38 - 6 = 32. Read it aloud so a child watching the recording can mark their own work. Ask: who has more? (Mei) So who has the smaller number? (Siti). Fewer means take away.

slides.title: Who is in the group?

blocks.head: STORY
items: Ravi is in a line. There are 5 children in front of Ravi and 2 behind him. How many children are in the line?

blocks.text: Count Ravi too!

slides.note: A reading trap. Show the line on a shared whiteboard, a blank slide or with counters: 5 children, then Ravi, then 2 children. 5 + 2 = 7 leaves Ravi out, so add 1 more: 8 children. Ask: who is in the group? Always check you counted everyone, including the person in the story. This is the taught idea for the Think harder page.

slides.title: Step it out

blocks.text: Lean forward for add. Lean back for take away.
Where do you end up? Sip some water.

slides.note: Three minutes. Stand up on camera. Call each move; children lean forward and back in the space they have (no stepping backwards): add 3, take away 2, add 4, take away 5. Say each count clearly; children count quietly along. After the four moves, everyone is back at the chair: 3, 1, 5, 0. No equipment; keep it gentle for small spaces.

slides.note: Read questions 1 to 3 aloud, twice. Children work on their own; the tutor looks around the gallery and asks how do you know. Wait 10 seconds before helping. After question 3 any child may carry on or try Think harder. Question 1 shows the steps; question 2 asks for the two sentences; question 3 asks which sentences to circle.

slides.title: Check page 1
slides.note: Read each answer aloud so a child watching the recording can mark their own work. Question 1: 10, 10 and 16, 16. Question 2: 49 then 39. Question 3: circle 25 + 10 = 35 and 35 - 3 = 32; Ravi has 32. Never ask a child to show a wrong answer to the group.

slides.title: Workbook page 2: Start here

blocks.text: Questions 4 to 6. About 7 minutes

slides.note: Read question 4 aloud: write + or - for each story. Read question 5 aloud, twice: Ben has more than Ali, so find Ben first. Read question 6 aloud: it is a spot-the-mistake. Children may draw counters to decide. Children who finish page 2 may choose Think harder, Go further or the Investigation, or finish at home.

slides.title: Check page 2
slides.note: Question 4: plus, minus, minus, plus. Question 5: Ben has 33, together 56. Question 6: Siti added the 10, but children who get off leave the bus; the right steps are 30 - 10 = 20 and 20 + 4 = 24. Read each answer aloud. Never ask a child to show a wrong answer to the group.

rows: Our idea in a new setting
Finish and check your own work

blocks.text: Everyone may choose. Pages 3 to 5 can go home.

slides.title: Back to the sneak-peek

blocks.text: Ben has 3 more than Ali, and Ali has 4.

Does it matter which comes first?

start.text: Ben has 30 cards. He gives 20 cards away. After that, he gets 6 more cards.
start.hint: Say what happens first. Gives away means take away. Gets more means add.
start.solution: First, Ben gives away 20, so we take away: 30 - 20 = 10. Then he gets 6 more, so we add: 10 + 6 = 16. Ben has 16 cards now.
mistakes: Adding the 20 (30 + 20) because 20 is in the story.
Using 30 again in Step 2 instead of the 10 left after Step 1.

start.text: Mei has 42 stickers. She gets 7 more stickers. Then she gives 10 stickers to Ali. Write one number sentence for each step.
start.hint: Use counters or draw it. What happens first? Then what happens next?
start.solution: Step 1: she gets 7 more, so add: 42 + 7 = 49. Step 2: she gives 10 away, so take away: 49 - 10 = 39. Mei has 39 stickers now.

start.text: Ravi has 25 pencils. He buys 10 more pencils. Then he loses 3 pencils. Circle the 2 number sentences that fit the story.
start.hint: Buys more means add. Loses means take away. The second step starts from the answer to the first.
start.solution: Step 1: buys 10 more, so 25 + 10 = 35. Step 2: loses 3, so 35 - 3 = 32. The sentences 25 - 10 = 15 and 35 + 3 = 38 use the wrong sign.
mistakes: Circling 25 - 3 = 22 because both numbers are in the story.
Circling a sentence with the wrong sign.

parts.text: Ali has 8 shells. He finds 5 more shells. 8 [] 5 = 13
Siti has 9 sweets. She eats 3 sweets. 9 [] 3 = 6
Mei has 10 stickers. She gives away 4 stickers. 10 [] 4 = 6
12 children stand in a line. 6 more join. 12 [] 6 = 18

start.hint: Does the story word make the number greater or smaller? Gets more makes it greater.
start.solution: Finds more means add (+). Eats means take away (-). Gives away means take away (-). Join means more, so add (+).
mistakes: Choosing + for gives away because there is a number in the sentence.

start.text: Ali has 23 marbles. Ben has 10 more than Ali. How many marbles do they have altogether? Use counters if you like.
start.answer: Step 1: Ben has 23 + 10 = 33. Step 2: 23 + 33 = 56. They have 56 marbles.
start.hint: Read it twice. First find how many Ben has. Then put Ali and Ben together.
start.solution: Step 1: Ben has 10 more than Ali, so 23 + 10 = 33. Step 2: altogether means add Ali and Ben: 23 + 33 = 56 marbles.

start.text: A bus has 30 children. 10 children get off. Then 4 children get on. Siti writes 30 + 10 = 40 for Step 1.

parts.text: Is Siti right? Circle Yes or No.

start.answer: No. Get off means take away: 30 - 10 = 20. Then 20 + 4 = 24. There are 24 children.
start.hint: Who leaves the bus? Do they make the bus fuller or emptier?
start.solution: Children who get off leave the bus, so Step 1 is a take away: 30 - 10 = 20. Siti added the 10. Then 4 get on, so add: 20 + 4 = 24.

think.text: Ravi has 15 marbles. He has 3 more marbles than Mei.
think.answer: Mei has 12 marbles. Together they have 27.
think.hint: Ravi has more, so Mei has fewer. Draw two groups of counters and compare them.
think.solution: Ravi has 3 more than Mei, so Mei has 3 fewer than Ravi: 15 - 3 = 12. Together: 15 + 12 = 27 marbles.
mistakes: Adding 15 + 3 = 18 because the word more is there.

think.text: Mei is in a line to buy lunch. There are 6 children in front of her and 4 children behind her. How many children are in the line?

parts.text: There are ___ children in the line.

think.hint: Draw the line of children. Did you draw Mei too?
think.solution: The children in front are 6 and behind are 4: 6 + 4 = 10. Mei is in the line as well, so 10 + 1 = 11 children.

think.text: Ben has 12 marbles. Mei has 5 more marbles than Ben. Siti has 3 fewer marbles than Mei. How many marbles does Siti have?
think.hint: Find Mei first. Then Siti has fewer than Mei.
think.solution: Step 1: Mei has 5 more than Ben: 12 + 5 = 17. Step 2: Siti has 3 fewer than Mei: 17 - 3 = 14 marbles.
mistakes: Taking 3 from 12 (Siti is compared with Mei, not Ben).

think.text: Ali has 12 stickers. He gives 7 stickers to Mei. Then he gives 8 stickers to Ben.

parts.text: After giving 7 to Mei, Ali has ___ stickers left.
Can Ali give 8 stickers to Ben? Circle Yes or No.

think.answer: 5 stickers left; No, the story cannot happen.
think.hint: Do the first step. How many stickers are left? Is that enough for the second step?
think.solution: Step 1: 12 - 7 = 5, so Ali has 5 stickers left. Step 2 needs 8 stickers, but 5 is less than 8. Ali cannot give Ben 8, so this story can not be true. A story step can be impossible, so check each step.
mistakes: Writing 12 - 7 - 8 and getting an answer without noticing 5 is less than 8.

go.text: A shop has 60 pencils. It sells 24 pencils on Monday and 15 pencils on Tuesday. On Wednesday, a box of 30 pencils comes in. Write one number sentence for each step.
go.answer: Step 1: 60 - 24 = 36. Step 2: 36 - 15 = 21. Step 3: 21 + 30 = 51. The shop has 51 pencils.
go.hint: There are three things that happen, so there are three steps. Write one number sentence for each.
go.solution: Monday: 60 - 24 = 36. Tuesday: 36 - 15 = 21. Wednesday a box comes in, so add: 21 + 30 = 51 pencils.
mistakes: Adding 24 and 15 and taking that from 60 but forgetting the box.

go.text: Step 1: 25 + 10 = 35. Step 2: 35 - 8 = 27. Write a story that fits both steps. End your story with a question. Many stories are right.
go.answer: Any story where 25 grows by 10 and then 8 are taken away, and the question asks how many now. The answer is 27.
go.hint: Pick who and what. Step 1 adds 10. Step 2 takes away 8. What could 25 be?
go.solution: For example: Ali has 25 stickers. He gets 10 more. Then he gives 8 to his sister. How many stickers does Ali have now? 25 + 10 = 35, 35 - 8 = 27.
mistakes: A story where the second step starts from 25 instead of 35.

go.text: Mei, Ali and Ben have 70 shells altogether. Mei has 25 shells. Ali has 10 more shells than Mei. Write one number sentence for each step. How many shells does Ben have?
go.answer: Ali has 35. Mei and Ali have 60. Ben has 10 shells.
go.hint: Find Ali first. Then find how many Mei and Ali have together.
go.solution: Step 1: Ali has 25 + 10 = 35. Step 2: Mei and Ali have 25 + 35 = 60. Step 3: Ben has the rest: 70 - 60 = 10 shells.

investigation.title: Does the order matter?
investigation.first: Start at 20. Add 10, then take away 5. Start again at 20. Take away 5 first, then add 10. Is the answer the same?
investigation.text: Pick your own numbers. Try both orders. Is the answer always the same? When can one order not work?
investigation.answer: Both orders give the same answer (20 + 10 - 5 = 25 and 20 - 5 + 10 = 25) whenever both orders can be done. But the order can matter for what you are allowed to do: from 4 you cannot take away 6 first, though 4 + 10 - 6 = 8 works. So: the answer is the same, but you cannot take away more than you have.
val: same answer when both orders can be done
cannot take away more than you have
investigation.look_for: A child who tests several numbers, says what they notice, and finds a case where taking away first is not possible (start 4, take away 6).
mistakes: Testing only one example and saying always.
Thinking the answer changes because the numbers change places.

talk.question: Siti has 20 stickers. Ali has 5 fewer stickers than Siti. Ravi says Ali has 25 stickers. Do you agree? Use counters to explain.
talk.answer: No. Fewer means less. Ali has 5 fewer than 20, so Ali has 20 - 5 = 15 stickers. Siti has more than Ali, so 25 cannot be right.
talk.look_for: A reason that uses the word fewer or less and shows 20 with 5 taken away (not just because 25 is too big).

exit.text: A bus has 25 children. 10 children get off. Then 3 children get on. How many children are on the bus now?
exit.solution: Get off means take away: 25 - 10 = 15. Get on means add: 15 + 3 = 18.

exit.text: Ben has 6 stickers. Mei has 5 more stickers than Ben. How many stickers does Mei have?
exit.solution: Mei has more than Ben, so add: 6 + 5 = 11.

exit.text: Siti has 20 beads. Ali has 7 fewer beads than Siti. How many beads does Ali have?
exit.solution: Ali has fewer, so take away: 20 - 7 = 13.
mistakes: Writing 27 (adding because the number 7 is there).

items.q: Make up your own two-step story with one add and one take away. Write the question. Solve it, then check each step.

menu.title: Is it always true?
menu.tutor: Mei says: you can add and take away in any order and get the same answer. Is that always true? Try 20 + 10 - 5, then 20 - 5 + 10, then 4 - 6 + 10.
menu.rec: Recording: pause. Try 20 + 10 - 5 and 20 - 5 + 10. Then try 4 - 6 first. What do you notice?
menu.answer: 20 + 10 - 5 = 25 and 20 - 5 + 10 = 25: the same. But from 4 you cannot take away 6 first. The answer is the same when both orders can be done.

questions.skill: Tens and ones: read a picture of sticks in tens and ones
questions.text: Count the sticks. Fill in the blanks.
questions.say: Gate 1. Look at the sticks. How many bundles of ten, and how many single sticks? Write them. Then write how many sticks there are altogether.
questions.solution: 3 bundles of ten is 30, and 9 singles makes 39.
questions.partly: Two of the three correct (for example 39 but the tens and ones swapped).
mistakes: Counting each bundle as one stick (3 + 9 = 12).

questions.skill: Number line (the number the arrow shows) and counting on in tens (Lessons 2 and 4)

parts.text: Look at the number line. The arrow is pointing to ___.

questions.say: Gate 2. Fill in the blanks. Part a: look at the number line. Which number is the arrow pointing to? Part b: count on in tens and write the next number: 14, 24, 34.
questions.solution: The arrow is just after 66 and just before 68, so it points to 67. In 10s: 14, 24, 34, 44 (the tens digit goes up by 1 and the ones digit stays 4).

questions.skill: Make the greatest number from two cards
questions.text: Look at the two cards. Use both cards to make the greatest number you can.
questions.say: Gate 3. You have two cards, 3 and 8. Use both cards to make the greatest number you can. Write it.
questions.solution: Two numbers can be made: 38 and 83. 83 has 8 tens and 38 has 3 tens, so 83 is the greatest.
questions.partly: 38 written (the other number made from the cards).

questions.skill: Add by making a ten, then with a tens number
questions.text: Look at the ten frames. Fill in the missing numbers.
questions.say: Gate 4. Look at the ten frames: 7 and 5. Write 7 plus 5. Then write 37 plus 5.
questions.solution: 7 + 3 = 10, and 2 more makes 12. 37 + 3 = 40, and 2 more makes 42.
mistakes: (b) 32 or 312 (joining digits or forgetting the tens).

questions.skill: Jump in tens (52 + 30) and take away tens and ones (74 - 31) (Lessons 6 and 7)
questions.say: Gate 5. Part a: write 52 plus 30. Part b: write 74 take away 31.

questions.skill: Equals as a balance: a box number
questions.say: Gate 6. Fill in the missing number in each box. Part a: 8 plus 4 equals 6 plus box. Part b: 60 plus 10 equals 50 plus box.
questions.solution: (a) 8 + 4 = 12, and 12 is 6 + 6, so the box is 6. (b) 60 + 10 = 70, and 70 is 50 + 20, so the box is 20. Both sides must have the same total.
mistakes: (a) 12 (writing the total of the left side).
(b) 70 (the total instead of the missing number).

questions.skill: Draw a line of a given length, then find a length 4 cm longer

parts.text: Draw a line 6 cm long. Start at the dot.
parts.ans: A line from the dot, 6 cm long (5.7 to 6.3 cm)

parts.text: A line 4 cm longer than your line is ___ cm long.

questions.say: Gate 7. Use your ruler. Part a: draw a line 6 centimetres long, starting at the dot. Part b: write how long a line 4 centimetres longer than your line is.
questions.solution: Put the 0 mark of the ruler on the dot and draw to the 6 mark. A line 4 cm longer is 6 + 4 = 10 cm.
questions.right: The line is about 6 cm (5.7 to 6.3 cm; accept 5.5 to 6.5 cm if the photo is not clear) and 10 is written.
questions.partly: Only the line about right, or only the 10 written (a line within 0.5 cm of 6 cm counts if the photo is not clear).
mistakes: Starting the line at 1 on the ruler (a 5 cm line).

questions.skill: A two-step story, one operation per step
questions.text: Mei has 35 stickers. Ali gives her 10 more stickers. Then she gives 3 stickers to Ben. Write one number sentence for each step. The last number you write is how many stickers Mei has now.
questions.say: Gate 8. Read it twice. Mei has 35 stickers. Ali gives her 10 more stickers. Then she gives 3 stickers to Ben. Write a number sentence for Step 1 and for Step 2. The last number you write is how many stickers Mei has now.
questions.solution: Step 1: she gets 10 more, so add: 35 + 10 = 45. Step 2: she gives 3 away, so take away: 45 - 3 = 42.
questions.right: Both step sentences have the right operation and numbers (any clear layout) and the second ends with 42.
questions.partly: One correct step sentence, or both sentences right with one slip in the arithmetic, or only the answer 42 without steps.
mistakes: 32 (taking the 10 away from 35 and adding 3 or similar).

optional.skill: Reading trap: who is in the group
optional.text: Think harder (optional). Ali is in a line. There are 5 children in front of him and 3 children behind him. How many children are in the line?

parts.text: There are ___ children in the line.

optional.say: The secret cave has one more puzzle, and it is optional. You may skip it. Ali is in a line. There are 5 children in front of him and 3 children behind him. How many children are in the line?

optional.note: Never marked and never counted. Whether the child tried it adds one neutral phrase to the line for the grown-up; a skipped cave adds nothing.

give: A week before: send the grown-up note (L10_Quest_Parent_Note.pdf) and the Quest Log (L10_Quest_Log.pdf) with the lesson materials. Families print the Quest Log at 100%, keep it closed in an envelope and find a quest partner (a grown-up or a brother or sister). A family with no printer tells you: arrange another way (for example the make-up slot).

Tell the group in the opening and at slide s-quest1: this is Mi's Challenge Quest, a game with Mi. Everyone works on their own paper with a quest partner beside them. It is not a race, a gate may be skipped, and nothing is shown to the group.

Start at minute 63 (after the break and the workbook) and finish by minute 83. Children open the Quest Log only when you say. The paper lies flat on the table and is never held up. The quest partner may talk about how to start and ask 'how do you know?', but does not give answers. Cameras may be on or off. Use your own watch out of sight of the camera: no clock, countdown or timer is ever shown to the children.

Read each page aloud, one gate at a time, then leave quiet working time: about 2 minutes for page 1, 3 for page 2, 4 for page 3 and 3.5 for page 4. After each page say that the gates are open and Mi swims on, whatever the answers. Say nothing about right or wrong, and read no answers. A middle child needs about 16 minutes in all; a slower child may use the 5 flex minutes.

Allowed: fingers, counters, the kit squares, the ruler for gate 7, and talk with the quest partner. Not allowed: a calculator, a grown-up giving answers, looking at the workbook. A child who finishes early turns the Quest Log over and draws quietly. Colouring a stone on the quest map means I had a go, never I got it right.

After page 2, take a one-minute stretch (stand, shake out, sip water). After page 4, show slide s-quest2. Do not collect or look at any Quest Log. A child still writing may use the flex minutes; nothing new is started there. While children work, notice (do not write on the shared screen) how they start: counters, drawing, number line, talking to the partner.
after: Same day: the grown-up takes ONE clear photo of each of the 4 pages (page flat, taken straight from above, the whole page in view including the 10 cm bar on page 4, and the name on each page) and sends them to the program's business WhatsApp, +65 9880 5962, and to no other number. If the photo is not clear, ask the grown-up (not the child) for a clearer one, or rely on the answer to part (b). Nothing is written on the child's paper, nothing is added up and no order of children is made. Nothing about the quest goes back to the child or the group except thanks.

Write ONE line for each grown-up from your notes (section 7): what we saw, in plain words, and one small next step if it helps. It is sent to the parent only. No marks, no x out of 10, no ranking, no comparison with other children, no prediction.

Fill in the group advice sheet (section 6): what several children were still working on, with no names, and what you will do in the first lessons of next term. It is kept for next term's tutor and is never shown to families.

Once the line is sent, save the photos to the program's private file store and delete them from the business WhatsApp chat. The program keeps the photos for 90 days after the program ends, then deletes them, as the privacy notice says. Delete each child's notes sheet when the line is sent (keep only the line in the family file, and the group advice sheet). Never forward the photos or save them to a personal phone or any other device.
